verdict.rationale: Dagster's own docs cover event-driven rules in two ways: sensors take action in response to internal or external events, and Declarative Automation conditions launch asset executions based on asset and dependency status. Changelog entries show automation-condition evaluation is actively developed, and Dagster+ alert policies add event-triggered notifications. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of event-triggered automation, detailed documentation of how sensor rules are defined and what event sources they support.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Sensors enable you to take action in response to events that occur either internally within Dagster or in external systems.
Declarative Automation is a framework that uses information about the status of your assets and their dependencies to launch executions of your assets.
Automation condition evaluations now explain history-dependent conditions (since, newly_true, newly_missing) by showing the remembered values that determined them
Dagster+ alerts can notify you of critical events occurring in your deployment so you can catch potential issues early
